# Frontend Html Sanitizer

Use only the rules that apply to the current consumer task.

## Contents

- [Sanitized rich text instead of trusted HTML](#sanitized-rich-text-instead-of-trusted-html)

## Sanitized rich text instead of trusted HTML

Render untrusted HTML such as pasted e-mail or Word content through nhSanitizeHtml or NhHtmlSanitizer from @newheap/platform-common/sanitize, keep the strict allow-list, and use the deprecated safeHtml only for HTML the application wrote itself.

## Preferred approach

Show HTML that the application did not write itself, such as pasted e-mail or Word content, a
rich-text field or text from another system, through the HTML sanitizer of the optional
`@newheap/platform-common/sanitize` entry point. Install its optional peer `dompurify` (`^3.4.0`);
applications that do not import the entry point need not install it. Import the standalone
`NhSanitizeHtmlPipe` and bind `[innerHTML]="message.body | nhSanitizeHtml"`. In code, inject
`NhHtmlSanitizer` and call `sanitize(html)` for the sanitized string, for example before you store
or send it, or `sanitizeToSafeHtml(html)` for a value to bind.

The default allow-list keeps the structure and inline formatting of rich text: paragraphs,
headings, lists, tables, quotes, links and emphasis, with only `href`, `title`, `lang`, `dir` and the
table and list attributes. It drops `class`, `id`, `style`, images and comments, so pasted content
neither takes over the application's styling nor loads tracking images. Scripts, styles, event
handlers, frames, embedded objects, forms and their controls, SVG and MathML are always removed,
also when an allow-list names them. URL attributes keep only `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `tel`
URLs; relative URLs are refused unless `allowRelativeUrls` is set, and a URL that starts with `//`
or `/\` is always refused. Every link gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and, unless
`openLinksInNewTab` is `false`, `target="_blank"`.

Change the allow-list only where the content needs it. Each option replaces its default list, so
extend a default by spreading it, for example
`allowedTags: [...NH_HTML_SANITIZER_DEFAULT_TAGS, 'img']` with `src` and `alt` in
`allowedAttributes`. Provide application-wide options with `provideNhHtmlSanitizer({...})` in the
root providers; a component or route may provide its own for the `nhSanitizeHtml` pipes in its
templates; the pipe argument and the options of a `sanitize` call win over both.

During server-side rendering there is no DOM, so the sanitizer escapes the HTML and it shows as
text until the browser renders the sanitized version; `isSupported` tells which case applies. Text
without markup comes back unchanged.

`safeHtml` (`SafeHtmlPipe`) is deprecated and unchanged. It calls
`DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml`, which bypasses Angular's sanitizer instead of sanitizing,
so scripts, event handlers and `javascript:` links in its value run in the application. Keep it
only as a low-level alternative for HTML the application wrote itself.

## Avoid

- Binding user, pasted or imported HTML through `safeHtml`, `bypassSecurityTrustHtml` or a
  sanitizer of your own built on regular expressions.
- Adding `style`, `class`, `id` or images to the allow-list for pasted content without a reason;
  styles and classes let content cover or imitate the application, and remote images reveal who
  read it.
- Allowing relative URLs for content from outside the application, where they point into the
  application itself.
- Passing scheme names with a colon, such as `'https:'`; the sanitizer refuses them.
- Expecting the server render to show the formatted HTML; it shows escaped text.

## Verification

Render pasted e-mail and Word content and check that the structure and links stay while scripts,
event handlers, styles, frames, forms and `javascript:` links disappear and links carry
`rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Test a configured allow-list, including that an always-forbidden
element in it is still removed, and test the escaped text with `PLATFORM_ID` set to `'server'`.
Build an application that does not import the entry point without `dompurify` installed.
